messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> runtime-canary severity=high: sudden latency spike and elevated 5xx. p50 x3, p99 rising. metric: kernel_fallback_rate up from 0.5% to 18%. Paging @alicia.wu oncall and @josh SRE. https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/runtime-canary
alicia.wu: on it, looking at the dashboard now. seeing spike from 12:33 UTC
alicia.wu: initial read: kernel fallback spikes coincide with small batch sizes and lots of KV misses. nodes in canary group have CPU steal and io wait elevated
marc: that lines up with the deploy at ~12:32 — we rolled prefetch_v2 to canary (10% traffic). suspect new kernel path + prefetch interaction
josh: ok. let's minimize blast radius. plan: 1) flip feature flag for canary (kill-switch) 2) if no quick improvement, rollback canary 3) CS notify. who can flip the flag?
alicia.wu: I can. running toggle now. command:
```
/ff toggle prefetch_v2 --env=canary --value=false --author=alicia.wu
```
deploy-bot: Feature flag change requested by alicia.wu: prefetch_v2=false for env=canary. Applying...
deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: prefetch_v2=false (canary) :white_check_mark:
leo.eng: logs from a canary pod show repeated message:
```
[2026-03-15T12:33:15Z] warn kernel_fallback=true reason="unsupported-pipeline" batch_size=1 kv_miss=0.82
[2026-03-15T12:33:21Z] warn kernel_fallback=true reason="prefetch-path" batch_size=1
```
marc: yup kernel is falling back to generic kernels which are expensive per-token. that forces tiny batches and increases tail latency
josh: if flag flip doesn't stabilize in 60s, i'll trigger rollback. starting to pre-stage rollback command now
josh: rollback command I'll run if needed:
```
kubectl rollout undo deploy/runtime --to-revision=42 -n prod-canary
```
alicia.wu: dashboards starting to show partial improvement — kernel_fallback rate dropping, but still noisy. p50 trending down slowly
tina: support: we have an incoming alert from ACME corp reporting slow responses for their integration tests. Maria, can you confirm customer impact and message?
maria.cs: pinged ACME AM. they saw 20-30% slower requests on canary path. i've told them we're triaging and will update within 15m. i'll post a short note: "we've detected a regression in a canary deploy, mitigation in progress (flag kill + rollback ready)."
josh: okay I'm going to cut canary traffic to 0 to be safe. issuing rollback now.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by josh. Target: runtime deployment -> previous stable revision. ETA ~90s
alicia.wu: rollback progressing. pods terminating and new pods spinning up with stable image
leo.eng: post-rollback logs show kernel fallback messages drop to near-zero. batch sizes back to expected median 16
marc: metrics: p50 back near baseline in ~2m after rollback; p99 improved after 4m. KV hit-rate recovered.
alicia.wu: confirmed: canary is stable now, kernel_fallback_rate=0.9%, 5xx rate back to baseline. marking mitigation successful
incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED -> runtime-canary: mitigation=rollback + feature-flag kill-switch. severity: high -> resolved. Links: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/runtime-canary
josh: quick follow-ups: 1) reproduce failure with prefetch_v2 + kernel path in staging, 2) add automated canary guard to auto-toggle flag if kernel_fallback_rate>5% for 1m, 3) increase canary CPU/io guardrails, 4) postmortem
marc: i'll take the postmortem writeup with timeline and root-cause analysis, will assign action items. alicia, can you add the graphs and logs?
alicia.wu: on it. will also add the exact commands and rollout ids. cc: @deploy-bot for validating rollback playbook
tina: i'll patch CS notes and notify impacted customers that regression was limited to canary and rollback completed
maria.cs: ACME updated: communicated rollback and expect normal behavior now, will re-open if they see issues
alicia.wu: thanks everyone. keeping watch for 30m then closing the oncall handoff
josh: thumbs up. closing page once 30m stable. :thumbsup:
